_comment: OpenCatalogi capability matrix. Authored here; the cross-product index in market-intelligence is generated from it. Generated by a lane script on 2026-09-25 from rows, research citations and code-reading packs; see the PR body for the method, the row-source split and the column choice.
category: A self-hosted publication platform for Dutch public bodies that turns records held in OpenRegister into public catalogues and serves them to every channel that must read them: residents through a reading room (rendered by Portaliq), the national Woo-index through DiWoo sitemaps, data.overheid.nl and European portals through DCAT-AP, search engines through schema.org, and other organisations through a federated directory. Its category is the Woo publication platform (actieve openbaarmaking: xxllnc Publiceren, iprox.open, Decos JOIN Woo Portaal, Acato WooPortaal), and it overlaps the open data portals (CKAN, DKAN) on catalogue, harvest and DCAT publishing. It is NOT an enterprise metadata catalogue (DataHub, OpenMetadata, Collibra), a developer portal (Backstage) or an architecture tool (LeanIX), although the intelligence database links it to 79 competitors of which only 6 are open data portals and none is a Woo publication platform: the rest are enterprise architecture tools (20), developer portals and API gateways (21), IT service and asset management (19), metadata catalogues (7), Odoo modules (4), a board portal and the GEMMA Softwarecatalogus, whose software catalogue is Stackiq's category. If this paragraph is wrong, the columns and areas below are wrong with it: correct it here first.

capabilities.name: Mark a document as changed in the sitemap when its metadata changes, so the Woo-index harvests it again.

built.evidence: source read at a00f9f8 (lane tip 77fa61f7, no code change since): the sitemap index sorts by @self.updated and sets each page's lastmod to the newest updated time on it (lib/Service/SitemapService.php:202,230-239,280-286), so a metadata change does move the page entry. But each document's own <lastmod> is the file's published time, falling back to the publication's updated time only when the file has none (lib/Service/SitemapService.php:510-512,526), so a metadata-only change leaves the document's lastmod unchanged and the Woo-index has no per-document signal.

capabilities.name: Decide what happens to a harvested record when it disappears from its source: unpublish it straight away, or keep it until you act.

built.evidence: workspace checkout openconnector (integriq, development a9366588): when records vanish from a source, a full synchronisation deletes their targets (lib/Service/SynchronizationService.php:2793-2800), but each source can set deletionRatioThreshold, and above it nothing is deleted until someone reruns with forceDeletion (:3958-3985, forceDeletion read at lib/Controller/SynchronizationsController.php:363), with a SynchronizationDeletionGuardedEvent raised; incremental mode never deletes (:2793). Missing half: the choice is a ratio for the whole run, not a per-record 'keep until I act', and the action is delete, not unpublish. source read at a00f9f8 (lane tip 77fa61f7, no code change since): federated publications are read live from peers (lib/Controller/FederationController.php:81), so a record gone at the peer disappears at once with no choice.
